# Template migrations

One entry per template version, newest first. An entry lists what a project must do to move from the previous version;
"nothing" is a valid entry. An entry is written so that it can be used as the brief of a run.

The `## Unreleased` entry comes first. A commit that changes a template-owned path adds its line there in the same
commit: the date, the path (or its folder, ending in `/`) and the step a project takes; the release moves the entry
under its version number. `ops/tests/test_migrations_entry.py` (run by `uv run pytest -q`) fails when a path changed
since the last release is not named in the entry, and when a commit made since then changes a template-owned path and
adds no line to the entry (one made before its line existed is named in the entry by its short sha, as the back-fill
lines do; uncommitted changes count as the commit in the making). Exempt: this file, `CHANGELOG.md`,
`docs/template/VERSION`, the `omit:` prefixes of `docs/template/variables.yaml` and the template's generated records
(`.raw/`, `wiki/meta/`, `wiki/index.md`, `wiki/log.md`, `wiki/hot.md`). In a project's checkout (it keeps
`docs/template/README.md`) the test skips.

## Unreleased (after 1.8.0; written with each change; the release moves it under its number)
- 2026-11-02, `.claude/hooks/keep-cache-warm.py`, `packages/harness/tests/test_keep_cache_warm.py` (V23 of the verifier, on 4375e60): the `pretool` hook reads a `$(…)` or backtick pair inside double quotes as shell. The text of a quoted string is still data, except a `-c` or `eval` argument and such a pair: `out="$(timeout 900 uv run pytest -q 2>&1)"`, `x="$(sleep 600)"`, ``x="`sleep 600`"`` and a loop around a waiter inside `"$(…)"` are refused. The commit before blanked a double-quoted string whole, so a long wait inside a command substitution ran in the foreground for its whole time, which lets the prompt cache expire. A quoted string inside a pair is data again, and so is a heredoc body inside one, so `git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF' … EOF)"` with "for … do" and a waiter's name in the message still passes; a quote or a pair that never closes is ordinary text. The hook walks the command with a small scanner now, not one regular expression, since quotes nest inside a pair. A project that copies the hook gets the new verdicts; a plain quoted string is read as before. Two false positives are left: a heredoc body outside a pair, and unquoted prose with a `for`, a `do` and a waiter's name after it.
  measure: wrong verdicts of the `pretool` hook on the commands that hide a long wait or a loop around a waiter in `"$(…)"` or a backtick pair, and on the heredoc commit messages that must pass (`uv run pytest -q packages/harness/tests/test_keep_cache_warm.py`); before: 6 of the verifier's 10 probe commands wrong at 4375e60 (verify.md, V23), and 23 of the 104 tests fail on that hook (19 refusals, 4 passes); after: 0 of 10 and 0 of 104 fail, and 68 of 68 mutants killed (2 of the 68 survived the first tests, a `-c` body deep in a command and one near the start of a long command, and got their own tests). (this commit)

- 2026-11-02, `.claude/hooks/keep-cache-warm.py`, `packages/harness/tests/test_keep_cache_warm.py` (V3 of the verifier, on 595dc0c): the `pretool` hook gives the right verdict on three more kinds of foreground command. An option of `timeout` may carry a value (`timeout -s KILL 900`, `--signal KILL 900`, `-k 10 -s TERM 900`) and the duration after it counts; a `timeout N` or `sleep N` right after a quote or a backtick counts (`bash -c 'sleep 600'`, `sh -c "timeout 900 …"`, a command in backticks); a loop around a waiter needs its `do`, so the word "for" in prose before a waiter (`echo waiting for it; python3 -I _wait_for_log.py x.md 3`) is no loop and passes, while a waiter in the loop's condition (`until python3 -I _wait_for_log.py x.md 3; do …`) is refused as before. Before, the first two kinds ran in the foreground for the whole timeout, which lets the prompt cache expire, and a lone waiter was refused as a loop. A project that copies the hook gets the new verdicts; a command refused for another reason is refused as before. One false positive is left: prose with both a `for` and a `do` before a waiter reads as a loop.

  gates, hooks, run state, loops), `.claude/agents/` (the critic's stage `attack`; rules of the planner, writer,
  verifier and judge), `.claude/hooks/`, `.claude/skills/{new-chat-type,resume-stage,run-stage}`,
  `.claude/rules/harness.md`, `.claude/settings.json`, `schemas/` (stages, run state and manifest, stage result, gate
  verdict, loop), `templates/` (chat type, handoff, project brief, stage assignment), `docs/roles/` (the default and
  `fix` tables with `attack`, `returns_to` and `loop`; need-to-know; roles 1.9.0 to 1.11.0), `docs/loops/`,
  `docs/quality/` (`HAZARDS.md`), `ops/` (`bootstrap.py`, `insert-step-rules.py`, `machine-setup.py`,
  `night-tick.sh`).
- Steps: finish or abort the active runs; copy the template-owned paths above from the template at 1.3.0 over the
  project's; `uv sync`; `just catalog`; compare the project's own stage tables with `docs/roles/stages.yaml` and
  `docs/roles/pipelines/fix.yaml` (the stage `attack`, `returns_to`, the `loop` block) and move them to the new shape.
- Checks: `uv run harness validate`, `uv run harness docs-check`, `uv run pytest -q packages/harness`
- Breaks active runs: yes; a run's configuration is frozen (`config_changed`), and its stage table has the old shape

## 1.2.0
- Changed template-owned paths: `ops/bootstrap.py`, `ops/machine-setup.py` (new), `.claude/hooks/session-start.py`,
  `packages/harness/src/harness/{doctor,access,launch,resume,trust}.py` (`trust.py` new), `.claude/settings.json`
  (`python3 ops/machine-setup.py`, with `--user` and `--undo`, in `sandbox.excludedCommands`).
- Steps: nothing in the project. A role session no longer starts without the sandbox: on a Linux machine whose
  sandbox does not run (`harness doctor`), the next session start sets it up as this user where it can, or offers
  `python3 ops/machine-setup.py`, which asks for the administrator's password once.
- Checks: `uv run harness doctor`, `python3 ops/machine-setup.py --plan`
- Breaks active runs: no; a run open at the update reports `config_changed` (the settings are frozen) until
  `uv run harness refreeze --run <id>`

## 1.1.0
- Changed template-owned paths: `plugins/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, `.claude/settings.json`,
  `docs/roles/extensions.yaml`, `docs/roles/need-to-know.yaml`, `plugins/code-intel/scripts/`, `state.runs_root`,
  seven hooks under `.claude/hooks/`, `ops/night-tick.sh`.
- Steps: replace `harness-internal` with `<repo_name>-plugins` in the four configuration files; run
  `python3 ops/bootstrap.py --wait`; then, in the checkout, `claude plugin uninstall <plugin>@harness-internal
  --scope project` for every plugin of the old name (Claude Code binds the record to the checkout's path, so before
  any move). When no other checkout on the machine still uses `harness-internal`
  (`~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json`), `claude plugin marketplace remove harness-internal`, and delete
  `~/.claude/plugins/data/code-intel-harness-internal` if it is still there. Optional, to keep the runs in a container
  folder: finish the active runs; move the checkout into a folder of its own; run `uv run harness runs-root --init`
  there and move the old `<repo_name>-runs/` content into its `runs/`; `git worktree repair`; remove the moved `.venv`
  (it keeps the old paths) and run `python3 ops/bootstrap.py --wait`; accept Claude Code's trust dialog in the new
  folder.
- Checks: `uv run harness validate`, `uv run harness doctor`, `uv run harness runs-root`
- Breaks active runs: no; the optional move to a container: yes (their sessions and worktrees keep the old paths)
